- When sentiment is low or neutral (≤0.27), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >72.5), model often overshoots in the following 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment rises (≥0.44), model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is low; add 0.5–1.5% to first 5 days if sentiment <0.3.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >73.5 and true outcome drops below 71.5, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is rising and model forecast is below 70.5, consider a 1–2% upward adjustment to avoid underestimating bullish momentum.
